subject: Hands-on prompt review workshop — POC kickoff & scheduling
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — hands-on prompt review + load tests

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team (Devon and I) would like to move forward with a short POC to validate prompt routing and load behaviour for our chat flows. High-level ask: a 90-minute, hands-on workshop where we do a prompt inventory walkthrough, review guardrails/structured outputs, then run a few lightweight load tests against a staging endpoint.

Proposed goals for the session:
- Align on prompt categories and priority examples (billing, onboarding, troubleshooting)
- Walk through safety/guardrail rules and structured output schema
- Validate routing from our front-end to the model variants and observe latency/cost tradeoffs
- Run two small load profiles (burst ~100rps for 1 min; steady 10rps for 10 min) to sanity-check autoscaling and caching benefits

Would next Wed or Thurs afternoon PST work? I attached a first-pass prompt inventory export. If you can also share a short agenda and an expected list of attendees from your side, we can lock a slot.

Thanks,
Laura
Product Manager, AcmeCorp

Avery (SE) and Rishi (SRE/CS) are copied — Avery will lead the prompt workshop and structured output mapping, Rishi will own the load-test plan and staging endpoint integration.

I’m attaching a draft agenda and a short checklist for the environment prep (staging API key, CORS/access allowlist, test data flag). If you have a preferred slot, we’ll block the calendar and send an invite.

Agenda (draft):

- 15–55m: Prompt inventory walkthrough + mapping to output schema

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,

Thanks Devon — Thu 2026-03-11 15:30–17:00 PST works for us. Confirmed items for the session:

Pre-reqs from AcmeCorp (please provide before Thu):
- Staging endpoint URL + API key (scoped to test account)
- A short list (10–15) of priority prompts or a filtered CSV (preferably marked by category)
- Any required test data flags / CORS allowlist entries

What we’ll bring / who runs what:
- 15:30–15:45: Intros & goals (Marissa)
- 15:45–16:25: Prompt inventory review & structured output mapping (Avery)
- 16:25–16:45: Guardrails & moderation patterns (Marissa)
- 16:45–17:00: Load test execution + telemetry review (Rishi)

Load test approach (high level):
- Provide curl examples and a small script for blasting from your VPC; we’ll also kick off a parallel run from our side to compare latency and caching honors.
- Tracing: we’ll emit request ids and include per-token cost estimates in the response headers for the test run.

Attached is a short note on the load-test plan and a versioned agenda. If Acme wants us to run the heavy burst from inside their VPC only, we can hand over the script and let you run it — otherwise we’ll coordinate both sides.

A few internal notes: Rishi, please prepare KV cache warmup guidance and an example policy for routing prompt categories to cheaper variants for non-sensitive prompts.

Cheers,
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
